metadata.title: Texting My Own Number
metadata.subtitle: At 2:47 AM my own phone number texted me: "Do not let Devon inside—he is already in the crawlspace."

nodes.text: 2:47 AM · Your phone buzzes on the nightstand. The sender ID is your exact mobile number.
{{player_name}}, stay on the bed. Do NOT unlock the deadbolt when Devon knocks in 20 seconds.
Who spoofed my SIM? Devon is on a night shift at the hospital until 6 AM.

nodes.transcript: [static, frantic whispering] "Listen to my breathing, {{player_name}}. That is YOUR voice. Don’t open the door—he’s wearing Devon’s scrubs."

nodes.text: Look at the bedroom vent above your closet. I am waving my flashlight.

nodes.prompt: Three slow knocks hit your apartment door:

options.label: Text Devon to confirm where he is
options.player_reply_text: Devon, are you outside my door right now?

options.label: Check the peephole silently
options.player_reply_text: I’m checking the peephole right now. Don’t move.

nodes.text: Hey {{player_name}}, my shift ended early and my key snapped in the lock. Let me in, I’m freezing.
I saw the peephole darken, {{player_name}}. Open up—why are you staring at me without blinking?
Your hallway motion light flickers off. Both chat threads show "Typing..." at the exact same second.
Wait—the GPS ping just refreshed. Why is YOUR phone showing 3 meters above my ceiling?
Because someone is breathing inside my ceiling crawlspace right now...

nodes.headline: Who Is Outside—And Who Is Above?
nodes.teaser_text: Next: The cracked GPS map reveals your SIM has been underground for 3 days.

episodes.title: The GPS Pin Inside the Walls

nodes.text: 2:54 AM · You slide a chair against the doorknob. Your own number sends a live location pin.
{{player_name}}, stop messing around! Someone is standing at the end of the hall watching me.
Prove you’re Devon. What happened to our car in November?

nodes.transcript: [panting, metallic scrape] "We slid into a ditch off Route 9—now open the door before that thing reaches me!"

nodes.text: He memorized that from your cloud journal. Ask him what color your childhood scar is.

nodes.caption: GPS trace on my cracked screen: my phone signal is pinned inside Apartment 4C’s sealed wall cavity.

nodes.prompt: The knocking stops. Scratching begins inside the drywall:

options.label: Demand the voice in the vent show itself
options.player_reply_text: If you’re really me, drop something through the vent right now!

options.label: Call 911 and trace both SIM towers
options.player_reply_text: I’m dialing police dispatch to trace which SIM is cloned.

nodes.text: Look at the floor beneath the vent. I just dropped your silver watch—the one with the bent clasp.
Don’t call them yet! Dispatch will trace the tower to the crawlspace and he’ll seal me in before they arrive!
CLINK. A scratched silver watch hits your bedroom rug—the exact watch you thought you lost 3 days ago.
Too late, {{player_name}}. Why did you lock the real Devon out of his own apartment?
Wait... if that watch just fell from the vent, then what is on my wrist right now?!

nodes.headline: Two Identical Watches
nodes.teaser_text: Next: The watch on your wrist is running backward.

nodes.text: 3:02 AM · You stare at your own wrist. The silver watch you’re wearing has no serial number—and no pulse beneath the strap.
Stop staring at your wrist, {{player_name}}. Check your calendar. What date does your phone say?
November 14th. Why are you asking me that?

nodes.transcript: [crying, muffled thud] "Today is November 17th! You’ve been missing since the 14th! Look at the fridge—all the milk expired!"

nodes.text: Don’t listen to the vent. You never left this room on the 14th.

nodes.prompt: Your hands are shaking over the kitchen counter:

options.label: Open the fridge and check the date
options.player_reply_text: The milk carton expired 3 days ago... what is going on?

options.label: Check your own front camera
options.player_reply_text: I opened my front camera. Why won’t my face focus?

nodes.text: Because you haven’t eaten or slept in 72 hours. Every time you remember, the room resets to 2:47 AM.
Because a camera can’t focus on a reflection that’s missing its original! Look behind you in the lens!
The digital stove clock flickers: 03:07 -> 02:47 -> 03:07. A cold draft pours from the crawlspace hatch.
Pull the latch inside the hallway closet! If you don’t open it before 3:15 AM, I’m going to run out of air!
Wait... if YOU are suffocating in the crawlspace, then who is typing with my thumbs right now?!

nodes.headline: The Latch in the Closet
nodes.teaser_text: Next: Devon warns you what actually lives inside that crawlspace.

nodes.text: 3:09 AM · Rain slams against the fire escape. Devon slides a folded hospital badge under your front door.
{{player_name}}, STOP! Do NOT unbolt the crawlspace! I sealed that hatch myself on November 14th!
Why would you lock someone in our ceiling, Devon?! I’m calling the police!

nodes.transcript: [voice trembling, rain roaring] "I found you unconscious on the bathroom floor with TWO phones—and something wearing your face crawling out of the vent!"

nodes.text: I dragged one of you into the crawlspace and prayed I picked the right one.

nodes.prompt: Your hand hovers over the closet crawlspace bolt:

options.label: Ask Devon how he told us apart
options.player_reply_text: How did you know which one of us was the real me?!

options.label: Demand the voice above say our safe word
options.player_reply_text: If you’re really me, tell me the name of my childhood dog!

nodes.text: I didn’t know! One of you was bleeding red, and the other had cold grey dust on their fingertips!
You never had a dog, {{player_name}}! Wait—why did you just ask a trap question you used to test ME?
You glance down at your own phone screen. Fine grey dust smudges every letter you just typed.
Look at your fingerprints on the glass, {{player_name}}. Now look at the hallway camera feed I just sent you.
No... my fingers are freezing. Why aren’t my hands bleeding when I scratch the drywall?!

nodes.headline: Grey Dust on the Screen
nodes.teaser_text: Next: The hallway CCTV shows nobody was ever standing outside your door.

nodes.text: 3:14 AM · Your apartment intercom clicks on by itself. Static fills the living room.
Devon isn’t outside, {{player_name}}. Check the building CCTV frame from 10 seconds ago.
Then who slid the hospital badge under my door?!

nodes.transcript: [distorted, slowing down] "Let me in, {{player_name}}... I just want my apartment back..."

nodes.text: Devon moved out after the night of November 14th. The police taped the door.

nodes.caption: Hallway CCTV at 03:14 — completely empty right while "Devon" was knocking.

nodes.prompt: The crawlspace latch rattles from the inside:

options.label: Unbolt the crawlspace hatch
options.player_reply_text: I’m opening the hatch right now. Show me who you are!

options.label: Rip open the front door instead
options.player_reply_text: I’m opening the front door to see the police seal myself!

nodes.text: Stop! Look at the tape on the OUTSIDE of your front door first—it’s yellow crime-scene tape!
The door won’t open from inside because the police bolted it after they couldn’t find my body!
The crawlspace hatch swings open. A cracked phone tumbles out—with YOUR driver’s license taped to the back.
You finally let me out. Now turn around and look at the mirror behind you.
There’s nothing in the mirror... only the phone floating in midair...

nodes.headline: Zero Reflection
nodes.teaser_text: Finale next: Who died in the crawlspace on November 14th?

nodes.text: 3:21 AM · Sirens wail four floors below. Police boots thunder up the concrete stairwell toward 4C.
Read the date on the cracked phone, {{player_name}}. You died in the crawlspace when Devon locked the wrong one up there.
No... then who have I been texting all night?!

nodes.transcript: [calm, crystal-clear—your exact voice] "You were texting the living body that escaped with your keys. Thank you for unlocking the hatch so the police can finally find your bones."

nodes.text: Don’t tell the officers what really happened on Route 9.

nodes.prompt: Police flashlights sweep across the bedroom doorway:

options.label: Drop the phone so they hear it hit
options.player_reply_text: Let them find the truth in 4C.

options.label: Send the crawlspace GPS to 911
options.player_reply_text: Sending the full chat log and GPS trace to police dispatch now.

nodes.text: An officer picks up the cracked phone from the rug. He stares at the screen—and whispers your name.
Dispatch just confirmed the transfer! The officers are shining their lights straight into the open crawlspace!
At 03:30 AM, the police radio crackles: "Victim located in ceiling crawlspace. Suspect Devon arrested at hospital."
One last message appears on the evidence phone before the battery dies: "You can rest now, {{player_name}}."
The clock finally ticks to 03:31 AM. For the first time in 3 days, the hallway is silent.

nodes.headline: 03:32 AM · Bank Alert
nodes.teaser_text: Act 2 begins: The "dead" phone lights up—your face just withdrew $40,000 across town, and those bones in 4C aren’t yours.

nodes.text: 03:32 AM · One minute after the evidence phone died in 4C, your screen flashes white again—lit by a live bank security alert.
Did you really think 03:31 AM was the end, {{player_name}}? Your face just passed facial recognition at a downtown ATM.
How am I still typing if the battery hit 0%?! And why are you emptying my savings account?!

nodes.transcript: [typing fast, stunned] "Hello?! This is Detective Park, Cyber Unit. I’m holding the bagged evidence phone from 4C—how are new texts appearing on a dead SIM?!"

nodes.text: Tomorrow morning I’m driving to your parents’ house with your keys.

nodes.prompt: Detective Park is staring at the bagged phone in the forensic van:

options.label: Beg Detective Park to freeze your bank card
options.player_reply_text: Don’t hang up! Someone wearing my face just drained my bank account!

options.label: Tell Park to trace the twin SIM tower
options.player_reply_text: Trace my number’s duplicate IMEI right now—it’s moving downtown!

nodes.text: Whoa—I just pulled your banking log! A $40,000 wire went through 90 seconds ago from a terminal three miles away!
Impossible... two identical SIMs are active on the same tower grid! One is inside my evidence bag, and the other just checked into a hotel!
Static crackles inside the forensic van as your own phone number dials the evidence bag directly.
Nice try calling the cyber cops, {{player_name}}. By sunrise, nobody will believe you’re still in this world.

nodes.headline: Two Active SIMs
nodes.teaser_text: Next: Detective Park intercepts the $40,000 bank transfer—and catches your doppelgänger on ATM video.

nodes.text: 03:41 AM · Detective Park pulls the emergency fraud log on his tablet and sends you the live transfer slip.
Look at the timestamp on this transfer, {{player_name}}. The ATM camera shows YOU smiling—wearing a silver watch on the wrong wrist.
My watch runs backward when it gets near me! Where did the money go?!

nodes.transcript: [siren hum in background] "It paid for a private medical courier and a one-night suite at the Mercer Hotel. Wait—why would an imposter book a medical courier?"

nodes.text: Tell the detective to check the crawlspace body’s left collarbone—you don’t have a steel pin!

nodes.caption: 03:32 AM fraud log — $40,000 authorized via facial ID while the original phone sat sealed in evidence.

nodes.prompt: Devon just sent and immediately unsent a panicked message from the holding cell:

options.label: Tell Park to check the collarbone pin
options.player_reply_text: Wait! Devon says the body in 4C has a steel collarbone pin—I NEVER broke mine!

options.label: Ask Park to intercept the medical courier
options.player_reply_text: Trace that medical courier right now—it’s heading for a hospital!

nodes.text: Hold everything! The coroner just confirmed a titanium pin in the crawlspace body’s collarbone—that body is NOT you!
The medical courier dispatch is booked for St. Jude’s ICU—to transfer an "unidentified coma patient" at 04:00 AM!
A cold chill sweeps through the signal line—as if a hospital monitor just beeped directly inside your ear.
If those bones in 4C aren’t mine... then where is my real body right now?!

nodes.headline: Not Your Bones
nodes.teaser_text: Next: Detective Park storms the Mercer Hotel—and finds who checked into Room 404.

nodes.text: 03:54 AM · Rain hammers the glass canopy of the Mercer Hotel as Detective Park flashes his badge at the night clerk.
The night clerk swears "you" walked through the lobby twenty minutes ago carrying a black telecom case—and never blinked once.
A telecom case?! That’s the rusted signal repeater Devon and I found off Route 9 in November!

nodes.transcript: [shaky voice on precinct speaker] "{{player_name}}, listen to me! After Route 9, you collapsed with hypothermia—an ambulance took you to St. Jude’s! Then THAT THING walked back into 4C!"

nodes.text: Room 404 is just a relay station. You’re looking in the wrong building.

nodes.prompt: Detective Park reaches the fourth-floor hallway outside Room 404:

options.label: Warn Park not to touch any grey dust
options.player_reply_text: Put on gloves before opening 404—the grey dust carries the frequency!

options.label: Ask Devon whose body was in 4C’s ceiling
options.player_reply_text: Devon, if I’m in the hospital, whose bones did police pull out of 4C?!

nodes.text: Gloves on! The door is ajar—the room is empty except for a humming silver box and a room keycard taped to the mirror!
I swear I didn’t put anyone up there! The landlord said the tenant before us vanished three years ago—and he wore a titanium pin after a bike crash!
Inside Room 404, the humming box flashes "02:47" in crimson LEDs—and suddenly kills every hallway light on Floor 4.
My radio just died... and the hotel mirror has a fresh message scratched in grey dust: "ST. JUDE ICU · BED 9."

nodes.headline: ICU Bed 9
nodes.teaser_text: Next: The Room 404 keycard reveals how the Mimic hijacked your SIM—and how close it is to your hospital bed.

nodes.text: 04:05 AM · Detective Park bags the Room 404 keycard and snaps a macro photo of the magnetic chip taped underneath.
Look at the back of this hotel keycard, {{player_name}}. Someone soldered a micro-SIM booster onto the magnetic strip.
That’s why I can only talk through text! It turned my own SIM card into a digital cage while my body lies in a coma!

nodes.transcript: [footsteps running to elevator] "I’m calling St. Jude’s ICU right now to put armed security outside Bed 9—hold on, their switchboard is busy!"

nodes.text: I already forwarded the ICU phone line straight to my pocket.

nodes.caption: Room 404 Mercer Hotel keycard — modified with a cloned SIM relay mirroring your exact carrier frequency.

nodes.prompt: The Mimic is jamming St. Jude’s switchboard from inside the hospital:

options.label: Have Park unplug the Room 404 relay box
options.player_reply_text: Smash that silver relay box in 404—it’s boosting his jammer!

options.label: Use the relay to hijack hospital Wi-Fi
options.player_reply_text: Wait—don’t smash it yet! Reverse the relay so I can ping the ICU nurses!

nodes.text: CRUNCH! I smashed the silver relay—my police radio is back online! Dispatch is sending three cruisers to St. Jude’s!
Whoa—reversing the relay just pushed your text onto every pager in St. Jude’s ICU! The charge nurse just hit Code Silver!
Across the city, red strobe lights flare inside St. Jude’s fourth-floor ICU wing—locking the automatic fire doors.
Clever trick, {{player_name}}... too bad I’m already standing on the INSIDE of the fire doors.

nodes.headline: Inside the Fire Doors
nodes.teaser_text: Next: Devon finally reveals the full horror of what crawled out of the Route 9 culvert.

nodes.text: 04:18 AM · Driving 90 mph toward St. Jude’s, Detective Park patches Devon in on conference line from the station.
{{player_name}}, I’m sorry I lied about the ditch! When our car skidded off Route 9, your phone fell into a flooded telecom bunker under the road.
Why don’t I remember going down into a bunker?! All I remember is waking up in 4C at 2:47 AM!

nodes.transcript: [sobbing, rain on station window] "Because you went down to grab your phone and touched a live prototype relay! Your heart stopped for ninety seconds—and something copied your voice out of the static!"

nodes.text: That Route 9 bunker matches a sealed 2021 corporate black-site signal test.

nodes.prompt: Your memory flickers—cold water, a buzzing blue arc, and your silver watch stopping:

options.label: Ask Devon how to break the relay’s link
options.player_reply_text: If it copied me from the relay, what kills its signal?!

options.label: Ask why it hid the previous tenant in 4C
options.player_reply_text: Wait—why was the previous tenant of 4C already dead in our ceiling?!

nodes.text: Salt water or a hard EMP short! The night of the crash, when rain flooded the bunker, it screamed and dropped your watch!
Because the previous tenant was an engineer on that Route 9 project—he tried to seal the prototype inside 4C’s crawlspace before it replaced him!
Detective Park’s cruiser skids to a stop outside St. Jude’s ER entrance—just as the hospital’s main lights blink out.
Backup generators are kicking in—and the forensic lab just texted me the official DNA certificate from 4C!

nodes.headline: The Route 9 Prototype
nodes.teaser_text: Next: Devon calls from custody as the DNA mismatch clears him—and reveals the Mimic’s final timer.

nodes.text: 04:28 AM · Under red emergency lamps, Detective Park sprints up the hospital stairs toward Floor 4 while your phone rings.
I’m on Floor 3—stairs only, elevators are locked down! Keep texting me so I know your signal is still tethered to Bed 9!
I can feel the cold creeping into my hands again... every time the ICU monitor slows down, my letters blur!

nodes.transcript: [steady hospital monitor beep] "Beep... beep... Look how quiet you look in Bed 9, {{player_name}}. One flick of the ventilator switch and I keep your pulse forever."

nodes.text: The prosecutor just dropped my murder charge—I’m riding with the SWAT van to St. Jude’s!

nodes.prompt: You hear your own voice breathing right beside your comatose body:

options.label: Blast your phone ringtone at max volume
options.player_reply_text: I’m overriding the Bed 9 bedside tablet—max alarm siren NOW!

options.label: Speak the engineer’s Route 9 shutdown code
options.player_reply_text: Park! Read the serial stamped inside the 404 keycard over the PA!

nodes.text: I hear the bedside alarm screaming down the east hall! It bought us thirty seconds—I’m breaching the ICU doors!
Code "R9-ZERO-247" broadcasted! The Mimic just stumbled away from your ventilator clutching its ears!
The red corridor doors slam open—and Devon’s urgent call cuts straight through the hospital static.
The DNA report just cleared me 100%! Look at the forensic sheet Park is uploading—the dead engineer left a kill-switch note in his pocket!

nodes.headline: The Engineer’s Kill-Switch
nodes.teaser_text: Next: The certified DNA report proves who died in 4C—and how to force the Mimic back into the static.

nodes.text: 04:36 AM · Detective Park holds the ICU nurses’ station while uploading the official forensic report from Apartment 4C.
Confirmed: 0% match to you, 99.99% match to Marcus Chen—the missing telecom engineer who lived in 4C three years ago.
And what did his pocket note say?! Where did the Mimic run when you breached the ICU?!

nodes.transcript: [out of breath] "It fled down the service elevator toward the basement generator room! And Chen’s note says the Mimic dies if its host SIM is shattered inside a live magnetic field!"

nodes.text: If I cut the basement backup power, Bed 9’s ventilator stops on its own.

nodes.caption: Forensic DNA report — 0% match to {{player_name}}; confirms crawlspace remains belong to missing engineer Marcus Chen.

nodes.prompt: The Mimic just unsent its real plan—it’s cutting the basement generator to stop your ventilator:

options.label: Send Park straight to the MRI magnet room
options.player_reply_text: A live magnetic field—lure it through the basement MRI wing!

options.label: Alert ICU nurses to switch to battery pack
options.player_reply_text: Tell the Bed 9 nurse to lock the manual battery pack before power drops!

nodes.text: Brilliant! The MRI suite sits right between the service elevator and the generator—we can trap it inside the magnetic bay!
Charge nurse just switched Bed 9 to independent battery! Your heartbeat on the monitor jumped back to 78 BPM!
Deep beneath the hospital, heavy steel doors groan shut as the basement generator hum drops an octave.
I’m inside the hospital lobby with two officers! Heading down to Basement B1 to cut it off from the generator!

nodes.headline: Descent to Basement B1
nodes.teaser_text: Act 3 begins: The Mimic stalks the flooded basement corridor—wearing your exact face.

nodes.text: 04:47 AM · In ICU Bed 9, your fingers twitch for the first time in three days as your consciousness fights to pull back into your body.
Stop fighting the tether, {{player_name}}! If you wake up in Bed 9, I unravel into nothing!
You stole my watch, my bank account, and three days of my life! I’m taking my heartbeat back!

nodes.transcript: [echoing in tiled basement] "Park, I see it! Wait—it’s standing under the fluorescent lamp pretending to be an orderly, and its shadow isn’t moving!"

nodes.text: Devon, DO NOT approach it alone—wait for me to power up the MRI coil!

nodes.prompt: Your phone battery flickers 2% -> 1% as the Mimic lunges toward Devon:

options.label: Call your own number to disorient it
options.player_reply_text: Dialing my own number—feedback loop straight into its ear!

options.label: Warn Devon to throw saline water at it
options.player_reply_text: Devon! Grab the saline IV bag on the cart—salt water breaks its static!

nodes.text: It worked! Its phone shrieked like a siren—it dropped the crowbar and stumbled backward toward the MRI hallway!
Splash! Grey sparks exploded off its jacket when the saline hit—it’s retreating straight into the MRI bay!
The heavy copper-shielded door of the MRI room stands open—humming with a low, bone-rattling vibration.
We’ve got it cornered outside MRI Bay 2! Hold on, {{player_name}}—we’re bringing you home!

nodes.headline: Cornered at MRI Bay 2
nodes.teaser_text: Next: The hospital lockdown seals Basement B1—and the Mimic tries one last voice trick.

nodes.text: 04:56 AM · Basement B1 seals under emergency lockdown. Inside the MRI control booth, Detective Park watches the glass window.
Problem, {{player_name}}: the Mimic knows what the magnet does—it’s holding an iron IV stand to jam the MRI door open!
Wait—if you ramp up the magnet coil NOW, won’t it yank the iron stand—and my silver watch—straight into the bore?!

nodes.transcript: [switches clicking] "Only if Devon gets clear of the doorway first! Wait—the corridor lights just flickered and TWO people are standing outside the glass!"

nodes.text: Watch closely, detective. Shoot the wrong one and you kill your witness.

nodes.prompt: The Mimic just shifted its face to look like DEVON under the flickering red lamp:

options.label: Check which one has a silver watch
options.player_reply_text: Look at their wrists! The real Devon NEVER wears a watch!

options.label: Ask both what happened to our car in Nov
options.player_reply_text: Ask which side of the ditch we hit—only real Devon knows!

nodes.text: Got it! The one on the left has a gleaming silver strap—and zero reflection on the control-booth glass!
Left ditch—the passenger mirror snapped off! The other guy didn’t even answer, he’s lunging for the control glass!
CLANG! The magnetic field surges—ripping the iron IV stand out of the Mimic’s grip and slamming it against the wall.
You think a hospital magnet can erase me?! Let’s see what happens when I call your ICU bed directly!

nodes.headline: The Face-Shift Trick
nodes.teaser_text: Next: The Mimic calls you one last time as its voice begins fracturing into static.

nodes.text: 05:05 AM · Your phone vibrates violently—as if the Mimic is trying to crawl back through the speaker into ICU Bed 9.
{{player_name}}, it’s pulling itself away from the MRI door using the fire hose! Its skin is flaking into grey dust!
Don’t let it reach the hallway stairwell—if it escapes the magnetic bay, I won’t make it to sunrise!

nodes.transcript: [pitch distorting wildly] "Give... me... your... pulse! I paid the courier! I memorized your whole life! Why won’t my watch tick forward?!"

nodes.text: Security cameras in the basement just snapped two silhouettes at the magnetic bulkhead.

nodes.prompt: The Mimic’s voice is cracking—one last emotional blow could shatter its focus:

options.label: Remind it that it has zero real memories
options.player_reply_text: You only copied a cloud journal—you don’t even know my mother’s laugh!

options.label: Tell Park to trigger maximum 3-Tesla pull
options.player_reply_text: Detective Park—hit the 3-Tesla override right now while Devon holds the rail!

nodes.text: It froze! The backward watch on its wrist just snapped clean off and flew into the MRI tunnel!
3-Tesla active! Every coin, key, and the cloned SIM phone in its pocket just shot straight into the magnetic core!
A blinding blue arc cracks across the MRI bay as the cloned phone slams into the spinning magnet.
No... 02:47... 02:47... please don’t turn off the—[STATIC]

nodes.headline: Into the Magnetic Core
nodes.teaser_text: Next: Basement CCTV captures the final moment before the cloned SIM shatters.

nodes.text: 05:14 AM · Smoke drifts from the MRI bore. Detective Park pulls the basement security frame to verify the corridor is clear.
Wait—check the CCTV still from ten seconds ago! The cloned phone shattered, so why is there STILL a silhouette leaning against the far wall?!
Zoom in on the floor—it’s crawling toward the emergency intercom box on the wall!

nodes.transcript: [panting, footsteps splashing] "I see it! It’s barely a cloud of grey ash now, trying to plug into the hospital intercom jack!"

nodes.text: One wire... just let me touch one copper wire...

nodes.caption: 05:14 AM Basement B1 CCTV — faint silhouette collapsing beside the emergency wall intercom outside MRI Bay 2.

nodes.prompt: Its grey fingertips are two inches from the copper intercom jack:

options.label: Tell Devon to yank the wall intercom breaker
options.player_reply_text: Devon! Flip the red wall breaker above your head—kill the intercom!

options.label: Have Park hit the MRI quench discharge
options.player_reply_text: Park! Dump the secondary quench pulse—burn out every stray wave!

nodes.text: Breaker DOWN! The intercom sparked dead—and the shadow on the wall just collapsed into a pile of ordinary dust!
Quench pulse fired! Every static wave in Basement B1 flatlined to zero—nothing is moving on CCTV!
Silence settles over Basement B1. Upstairs in ICU Bed 9, the heartbeat monitor chimes in a strong, steady rhythm.
Wait... I can feel the warm cotton blanket on my hands... I’m not in the phone anymore.

nodes.headline: The Static Flatlines
nodes.teaser_text: Next: Upstairs in ICU Bed 9, your eyes snap open as the clock finally moves past 2:47.

nodes.text: 05:32 AM · Bright white ceiling tiles swim into focus. A nurse gasps as your eyelids flutter open in ICU Bed 9.
The charge nurse just radioed down—YOUR EYES ARE OPEN! Stay still, {{player_name}}, Devon and I are coming straight up!
My throat feels like sandpaper... but I’m actually typing with my own warm fingers on the nurse’s loaner phone.

nodes.transcript: [laughing through tears] "You made it! You actually beat that thing! And the bank just reversed the entire $40,000 fraud hold!"

nodes.text: Federal cyber-investigators just sealed the Route 9 culvert with concrete.

nodes.prompt: You glance at the bedside tray where the nurse placed your belongings:

options.label: Check the second hand on your real watch
options.player_reply_text: My real watch is ticking forward—5:35 AM, 5:36 AM. No more loop!

options.label: Ask Park to seal the Route 9 bunker forever
options.player_reply_text: Promise me nobody else ever finds that Route 9 repeater box.

nodes.text: And look at the mirror across from Bed 9—your reflection is staring right back, 100% solid and alive!
Already done—the Route 9 culvert is being filled with reinforced concrete as we speak, and Marcus Chen’s family finally has closure.
Outside the ICU window, pale pink dawn touches the rooftops as the night rain finally stops.
One last formality before we close the file—I’m bringing up the crushed cloned SIM so you can watch it go into the incinerator.

nodes.headline: Warm Hands, Forward Time
nodes.teaser_text: Next: Detective Park closes the cyber-incident file—and hands you a brand-new phone number.

nodes.text: 06:15 AM · Early sunlight warms the hospital courtyard. Detective Park steps into your recovery room holding a sealed titanium evidence tin.
The telecom carrier permanently purged your old number from the national registry. Nobody—and nothing—can ever dial it again.
Good riddance. And what about Apartment 4C? Please tell me we’re breaking our lease today.

nodes.transcript: [cheerful rustling] "Already packed both our bags and found a sunny top-floor place with ZERO crawlspaces and ZERO attics!"

nodes.text: Thank you for not giving up on me even when I looked guilty.

nodes.prompt: Detective Park opens the titanium tin showing the shattered, scorched SIM chip:

options.label: Sign the official destruction order
options.player_reply_text: Signed and dated—melt that chip down to slag.

options.label: Donate the recovered $40k reward to Chen’s kin
options.player_reply_text: Pass my thanks—and the city’s whistleblower stipend—to Marcus Chen’s family.

nodes.text: Stamped and archived. The Cyber Unit is officially marking Case 4C as resolved—with zero active anomalies.
Marcus’s sister just called our desk in tears—knowing his final note saved your life gave her real peace.
Your brand-new phone chimes softly—displaying a fresh SIM number and a single incoming test call.
Crystal clear audio, zero echo, zero static. Enjoy the sunshine, {{player_name}}.

nodes.headline: Case 4C Closed
nodes.teaser_text: Grand Finale next: One month later, a sunny morning coffee—and a phone that only rings with real friends.

nodes.text: 09:15 AM · One month later. Sunlight pours through the balcony of your new apartment as coffee brews in the kitchen.
Good morning, {{player_name}}! Grabbed two iced lattes and croissants from the corner bakery—buzz me up?
Buzzing you up now—and yes, I checked the lobby camera first just out of habit. Only one Devon down there!

nodes.transcript: [bright street chatter, laughing] "Fair enough! No backward watches, no grey dust, and definitely no 2:47 AM texts!"

nodes.text: Checking in one last time—your new SIM is 100% clean. Stay safe, kid.

nodes.prompt: You step out onto the sunlit balcony holding your warm mug:

options.label: Glance at your wrist—09:18 AM and moving
options.player_reply_text: Every second ticks forward in broad daylight. Best feeling on earth.

options.label: Text Detective Park a thank-you photo
options.player_reply_text: Coffee’s on us next weekend, Detective—thanks for pulling me back!

nodes.text: Doors opening on your floor—time to celebrate being 100% real and wide awake!
Deal! Make mine black coffee—and keep your phone charged above 20% from now on, {{player_name}}.
Sunlight gleams off your clean phone screen—reflecting only the bright blue sky and your own smiling face.
I used to dread every midnight ping. Today, the only voice on my line is my own—alive, free, and finally moving forward.
